title: [Bug]: Repeated GTP-U Error Indications can crash SMF during EPC bearer deactivation

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Establish an EPC PDN connection with a default bearer.
2. Have the SGW-U send two PFCP Session Report Requests containing an Error Indication Report for the same S5-U bearer before the first deactivation procedure completes.
3. The SMF processes both Error Indications independently and starts two deactivation procedures with `Reactivation Requested.`
4. Do not send Delete Bearer Responses from the SGW-C.
5. When the Delete Bearer transactions time out, each timeout starts its own PFCP Session Modification with `OGS_PFCP_MODIFY_REMOVE`  for the same bearer.
6. The first PFCP Session Modification Response removes the bearer. The second response attempts to remove the same bearer again.

### Logs

```shell
The captured SMF log shows two Error Indications for the same default bearer, EBI 5, received one millisecond apart at `10:29:36.405` and `10:29:36.406`.

Both reports start separate bearer deactivation procedures. After the first PFCP removal completes, the second PFCP Session Modification Response reaches `smf_epc_n4_handle_session_modification_response()` with no corresponding bearer and aborts at:


ogs_assert(bearer)
```

### Expected behaviour

While a bearer deactivation triggered by a GTP-U Error Indication is in progress, repeated Error Indications for the same bearer should be coalesced.

For the default bearer, the in-progress state should cover the entire PDN connection because its deactivation releases all bearers belonging to that session.

If a Delete Bearer Request for the default bearer times out, the SMF should release the entire PDN connection rather than removing only the default bearer.

The SMF should neither attempt to remove the same bearer more than once nor leave a live EPC session without a default bearer.

### Observed Behaviour

Every Error Indication starts a new bearer deactivation without checking whether one is already in progress. A single stale F-TEID can therefore produce multiple PFCP deactivations and multiple Delete Bearer Requests for the same bearer.

If the SGW-C does not answer those requests, every GTP transaction timeout sends a separate `OGS_PFCP_MODIFY_REMOVE`. The first successful PFCP modification removes the bearer, and a later response triggers `ogs_assert(bearer)` while processing the same bearer again.

In addition, `bearer_timeout()` does not distinguish the default bearer from a dedicated bearer. It removes either one using a single-bearer PFCP modification. Removing the default bearer this way leaves a live EPC session with an empty `bearer_list`, although EPC handlers assume that `smf_default_bearer_in_sess()` returns a valid bearer.
